hero.title: Tradux - Intelligente Übersetzungsbibliothek
hero.description: Entwicklerfreundliche Übersetzungsbibliothek, die mehrsprachige Inhalte in Ihren Projekten automatisiert. Die neue providerbasierte Konfiguration funktioniert mit OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google und Cloudflare und behält einfache Hooks für Vue und andere Apps bei.

callToAction.title: Beginnen Sie heute mit der Verwendung von Tradux

configuration.title: Konfiguration
configuration.description: Nach der Installation erstellt Tradux automatisch eine Tradux.config.json-Datei:

commands.all:
# Update all existing languages
npx tradux -u
commands.specific:
# Update specific languages
npx tradux -u es,pt

# Remove specific languages
npx tradux -r es,pt

updateVsTranslate.title: Update vs Translate:
updateVsTranslate.description: Update (-u) syncs existing language files with your default language, adding missing content and removing obsolete keys. Translate (-t) creates new translation files. Remove (-r) deletes language files and automatically updates the config.

features.useFor: Use for: Displaying current language, conditional logic

features.returns: Returns array of available language codes from config
features.useFor: Use for: Building language selectors, validation

seoInternationalization.title: SEO & Internationalisierung: Dynamische Meta Tags
seoInternationalization.description: Tradux erleichtert die dynamische Aktualisierung von Meta-Tags wie <html lang="..."> und <title> basierend auf der ausgewählten Sprache des Benutzers.
seoInternationalization.details: Sie können Meta-Tags dynamisch in Client-Side-Apps (React, Vue, Svelte, Vanilla JS) mithilfe von JavaScript oder auf dem Server mithilfe von SSR (Server-Side Rendering) mit Frameworks wie Express, Vite SSR oder AstroJS aktualisieren.

examples.title: Examples
examples.description: Tradux provides sub-path exports for your favorite frameworks. These hooks automatically fetch translations and provide a reactive state.

globalState.title: Global State & Reusability
globalState.description: Tradux uses a shared memory cache. If you have multiple translated components on a single page, you do not need to manage loading states for all of them.
globalState.details: Initialize Tradux once at the root of your app. Child components will instantly receive translations with zero network requests or loading flicker.

ssrRouting.title: SEO & Server-Side Routing
ssrRouting.description: For search engines to index your translated content, languages should be tied to the URL (e.g. mysite.com/es/about). Search engines ignore local storage and cookies.
ssrRouting.details: Tradux supports this natively. Instead of using setLanguage() (which relies on cookies), use your framework's router to extract the language from the URL and pass it directly to Tradux.
ssrRouting.expressDescription: When using custom SSR setups, you can use Tradux isolated instances to intercept requests, read the translation file on the server, and inject the correct html lang and title tags into your HTML before serving it to the client.

autoHealer.title: The Auto-Healer
autoHealer.description: Whenever you run a Tradux CLI command, the system validates your setup. If you manually delete a language file like pt.json, Tradux automatically removes it from your tradux.config.json array. If your folder paths get misconfigured, the CLI attempts to correct them safely.

differential.title: Differential Translation (.tradux-state.json)
differential.description: When you translate files, Tradux leaves a hidden .tradux-state.json file in your i18n folder to act as a state snapshot. When you run npx tradux -u, Tradux compares your current en.json against this snapshot and sends only the differences to the Cloudflare API.
